title: The Target is the Metropolitan Police Traffic Department
subtitle_source: subs_resolved/0971.txt (362 lines) + subs_resolved/0974.txt (328 lines), 690 lines total, both read in full. subs_resolved/0972.txt and 0973.txt do not exist in this dataset -- the middle two episodes (Yagi's murder scene itself, and the step-by-step narrowing from three traffic-violator suspects down to Aono) are only known via the recap dialogue and final confession in episode 974, not from a direct transcript.
notes: case_type: murder (x2) + kidnapping + attempted murder (same culprit, one continuous revenge spree). The old cases/ file's culprit call (Aono, s1) holds up -- episode 974's confession confirms him directly, no red-herring reversal needed there. Correction vs. the old file: the old file asserted a taser was used on both officers and that Yagi was 'thrown off a balcony'; neither detail appears anywhere in the two transcripts actually available (971, 974), and since 972-973 are missing from this dataset, that weapon/method claim could not be verified and has been dropped rather than carried forward unverified -- Yagi's death is recorded here with method left unspecified. The old file also missed that the culprit went on to kidnap patrolwoman Naeko Miike (to lure her superior Yumi Kitami, whom he'd also decided to kill after overhearing her name) and stabbed/impaled Sergeant Chiba on a booby trap while Chiba rescued her; both are modeled here as direct crime edges (kidnaps/assaults) rather than left as a notes-only aside, since they are the culprit's own continuing actions, not incidental cast business. Recurring detective-cast members who only investigate (Conan, Sato, Takagi, Kogoro, Megure, Haibara) are omitted by convention; Miike and Chiba are the exception because they are themselves directly targeted/injured by the culprit within this arc. Objects/clues describing the two dying-message decodings (no-parking-sign pun, phone-number legal-code reference) are drawn directly from Conan's on-screen deduction in ep974.

clues.desc: Momosaki's swing-set/no-parking-sign gesture and Yagi's '7155' phone-number message are two independently left dying clues that both resolve to the same name, Aono, by two different routes (a sign pun vs. an exact legal-code citation).

Of the three traffic offenders detained the same day, only Aono had a personal, emotionally charged history with Momosaki and Yagi -- they stopped him mid-emergency, on his way to a suicidal girlfriend -- while Akamine and Shiroyama had no comparable connection to the victims.

The four sets of seven finger-taps Chiba overheard on the phone match the syllable pattern of 'Twinkle Twinkle Little Star'; cross-referenced with Aono's remodeling job among several renovation sites nearby, this pinpoints the planetarium under renovation as Miike's hostage location.
